conviction_note: Nothing company-level the market has not seen: the bar is a 4-analyst Modular Finance consensus (Q3 adj. EBIT 11.3 MEUR) with Inderes publicly far below it at 9.3, the company gives no short-term outlook, and the small positives (USD translation, a buyback that can restart after the print, firm US office demand) only just outweigh the public EMEA/growth-deceleration risk. So p_up is 52 on a large scale (8%, set from new numbers and this name's own observed print reactions of -11.5%, +14.9% and +1.0%), which gives +0.32. The findings sum to +0.7; the gap is the scaled number putting almost no weight on proxies.

Framery gives no short-term outlook, only mid-term targets (>10% organic growth on average from the 2025 base, 25% adj. EBIT margin mid-term, ND/EBITDA <2.0x). Q2: revenue 51.4 MEUR (-3.7%), +6.9% excluding the largest single end-customer, adj. EBIT 12.0 MEUR (23.4%). EMEA sluggish (Nordics, DACH), AMER underlying +34%, first Michigan customer deliveries planned for Q3
Inderes Q3 preview: revenue 49.4 MEUR (-5%), adj. EBIT 9.3 MEUR (18.8%), against a Modular Finance consensus of 4 analysts at revenue 51.0 and adj. EBIT 11.3 (22.2%), EPS 0.10
Reorganisation: customer operations merged into Operations, change negotiations covered 43 employees, no cost-saving targets, 2 redundancies, one management team member leaves
EUR 10m share buyback (max 1.5m shares, 1.89%) running 15 Sep 2026 to 31 Mar 2027; about 140k shares bought by 2 Oct; 97,700 cancelled

adj. EBIT margin: consensus 22.2% against Inderes 18.8%. Price increases fully in effect and freight price lists repriced, against Michigan ramp costs and higher logistics/component costs. Unknown, roughly at consensus
none expected; the company does not publish a short-term outlook. A first FY27 comment would be a surprise in either direction
Gradus/Michigan ramp commentary and the 2027 financial calendar; qualitative
unknown; Q2 cash conversion was 106%, and the buyback is funded from cash flow

findings.finding: The bar is split: Inderes, the house most of Framery's retail-heavy holder base reads, put out a preview on 29 Oct with Q3 adj. EBIT at 9.3 MEUR (18.8%), 18% below the 4-analyst Modular Finance consensus of 11.3 MEUR (22.2%). So the effective expectation in the price likely sits below the formal consensus, and a print near consensus margin reads as a beat for part of the holder base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Observed on the real print dates (Yahoo daily bars): Q4'25 (16 Feb 2026) EPS 0.04 vs 0.08 est, -11.5%; Q1'26 (27 Apr) beat, +14.9%; Q2'26 (27 Jul) revenue miss but profit beat, +1.0% (+3.0% the next day). Profit surprises are paid in full on this name.

[We forecast Framery's adjusted EBIT at 9.3 MEUR in Q3 (Q3'25: 11.9 MEUR), an 18.8% margin (22.8%).] English table: 'EBIT (adj.) 11.9 / 9.3 / 11.3 ... Source: Inderes & Modular Finance, 4 analysts (consensus)'
findings.why_not_priced: The dispersion itself is public. What is not settled is which bar the price holds. The stock fell from 6.78 (15 Oct) to 6.12 (-6.7% over 20 days) and fell 2.3% on 30 Oct after the preview, which fits a partial move toward the lower bar. If the price fully held Inderes's 9.3, a consensus-margin print would be a clear positive; if it holds 11.3, this is worth 0.
findings.independence: Company's own statement that Q2 price increases were 'fully visible' and that freight price lists were repriced for fuel (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b24926fcef4cb4b97177bd6fe0615dc5e&lang=en&src=listed), which argues against a 4.6pp q/q margin drop

findings.finding: The EUR 10m buyback has filed no weekly purchase report since week 40 (the last release is 2 Oct, cumulative ~140k shares, about EUR 0.93m of EUR 10m). In other words it has been paused through the pre-results closed period, during which the stock drifted 6.6% lower, and it can restart with about EUR 9m of capacity once the report is out on 2 Nov.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback announcement on 8 Sep 2026: +4.5% that day. In week 40 the programme bought 41,997 shares, about 13% of that week's volume.
findings.why_not_priced: That a bid of about 13% of volume left the order book is visible only as the absence of weekly releases in the issuer feed (https://api.news.eu.nasdaq.com/news/query.action, Framery history read 2026-10-30). If the market were trading the restart, the pre-print drift on thin volume (10-45k shares/day) would not have happened. Most of the restart's effect lands after the window; only the first session counts here.
findings.independence: The share cancellation release of 14 Oct confirms the programme's scale and quarterly cancellation (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=badcab408e3de8282d9bc9985dbbb2e0c&lang=en&src=listed)

findings.finding: USD was stronger year on year through Q3 2026 (EUR/USD month-ends 1.159 / 1.134 / 1.116 against 1.169 / 1.173 / 1.157 in Q3 2025). AMER is about 35% of revenue and the cost base is mainly EUR, so translation adds roughly +1% to reported revenue and a small margin tailwind. In Q2 the FX effect was a headwind (-3.7% reported against -3.4% at comparable rates).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate history; FX was a small headwind in Q2 and drew no comment in the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts may already model it; it is small and is macro-to-company transmission. The Inderes preview names logistics and component costs but does not mention FX. If priced, the consensus revenue (-2.3%) would already embed it.
findings.independence: Company H1 report: 'The Company's primary cost base and reporting currency is the euro ... exposed to ... USD, SGD, and GBP' (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b24926fcef4cb4b97177bd6fe0615dc5e&lang=en&src=listed)

findings.finding: US office furniture read-through is mildly supportive. MillerKnoll FQ1 (Jun-Aug 2026): North America Contract orders -1.7%, but August orders up year on year, total orders +9% through the first three weeks of September, and International Contract orders +17.3%. HNI guided Q3 legacy Workplace sales to high-single-digit growth. Framery's AMER grew +34% underlying in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured; peers' prints have not visibly moved FRAMERY.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy (snippet_only, from secondary coverage). Pods are a niche inside office furniture, and the trends are public. Inderes already says US office demand is strong, so it is mostly in the bar.
findings.independence: HNI Q2 2026 call guidance for Q3 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/hni-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-31/)

findings.finding: Underlying revenue growth excluding the largest customer has slowed (H1 +11.1%, Q2 +6.9%), EMEA is shrinking on weak Nordics and DACH, and Q2 revenue missed expectations. Inderes cut its growth forecast and expects +5% underlying, while consensus revenue of 51.0 MEUR implies others expect more, so a revenue miss against consensus is the main public risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 revenue miss was offset by margin (+1.0%); the Q4'25 miss was -11.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and largely in the bar (Inderes flagged it; the stock has drifted down 6.7% in 20 days). It is kept small because it lands inside what the market was told.
findings.independence: Inderes preview: 'Kyseisen avainasiakkaan tilauksista oikaistu liikevaihdon kasvuprosentti on yhtiön pörssitaipaleen aikana ollut laskutrendillä' (https://www.inderes.fi/analyst-comments/framery-group-q326-ennakko-amerikan-veto-ja-euroopan-hiljaisuus)

findings.finding: The 26 Oct reorganisation (customer operations merged into Operations, 43 employees in change negotiations) set no cost-saving target and led to only 2 redundancies, so Q3/Q4 should carry no meaningful restructuring item affecting comparability.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +2.7% on 26 Oct, the day of the release.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and immaterial; it is filed for completeness and is worth 0.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive against a -6.7% 20-day run-up and a lean that is only the run-up term (+0.335). The direction agrees with that small lean, but nothing found is strong enough to beat the free control.
language_note: The Inderes Q3'26 preview was published first in Finnish (29 Oct 07:30 EET) and is translated into English on inderes.fi/en with the same numbers and the consensus table, so the Finnish source added no new number, only the original wording.

Finnish-language searches (muutosneuvottelut, osavuosikatsaus odotukset, Kauppalehti) turned up nothing the bilingual issuer releases did not already carry. As expected for a Helsinki issuer that publishes in both languages: nothing the English sources did not already carry.
lessons_applied: 'Right about the number, too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 7.5 to 8.0. New numbers, no pre-release, and this name's own observed print moves of 11.5 / 14.9 / 1.0 show it pays surprises in full; p_up is unchanged
'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth ~0': the public EMEA/growth-deceleration finding was moved from -0.3 to -0.2
Positioning: the truncated zero is stated as no anchor rather than as evidence nobody is short (positioning_check)
